newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Iraq crisis sparking review of Taiwan oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: Iraq crisis sparking review of Taiwan oil reserves.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday it would form a crisis management team to consider expanding the island's 30-day oil reserves as military tensions flare in Iraq.

"What we really worry about is whether Iraq will attempt to block oil transport routes out of the gulf region," spokesman Fang Yi-shan told Reuters by telephone after first reports of a U.S. military strike against Iraqi air defence sites.

"We will establish a crisis team to ensure our oil supplies in the case that large-scale war breaks out," Fang said. Fang said Taiwan had been maintaining a 30-day strategic oil reserve but would consider doubling that to 60 days to ensure energy supplies for the island's population and industry.
"We will follow this situation (in Iraq) closely," he said.
Fang said Chinese Petroleum, Taiwan's sole importer, would incur T$500 million in losses for each one U.S. dollar increase in the international price of oil.
Chinese Petroleum increased Taiwan's safety reserves to 60 days during the Gulf war.
Taiwan's island economy is almost completely reliant on imported oil, purchasing an average of 750,000 barrels of crude per day or about 275 million barrels a year.
Limited storage capacity, however, leave Taiwan vulnerable to oversupply if it acts too hastily or overreacts.
Chinese Petroleum was rebuked by parliament after the Gulf War because it had laid in too much oil in anticipation of a much longer conflict.
